header.name: Divi's Laboratories Ltd
header.source: NSE closing price (end of day, not live); 52-week range computed from daily highs and lows (NSE bhavcopy)

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Divi's Laboratories (NSE: DIVISLAB) makes active pharmaceutical ingredients, intermediates and nutraceutical ingredients; its consolidated revenue in FY26 was ₹10,560 crore.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: In the quarter to 30 Sep 2026, revenue was ₹3,676 crore, 35.4% more than a year earlier; the operating margin was 38.7% against 28.5%, and profit attributable to shareholders was ₹1,127 crore, 63.6% higher.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: On 8 Nov 2026, a Sunday special session and the first session after the result, DIVISLAB shares rose 7.52% while the NIFTY 50 fell 0.18% and the NIFTY PHARMA index rose 1.74%; allowing for the market's move, DIVISLAB's own move was +7.47%, about 5.29 times its usual daily variation.

claims.label: UNCERTAIN
claims.text: These numbers measure the move, not its cause: the result, the pharma sector's rise and any other news that day overlap, and nothing here separates them.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: At ₹11,203 (NSE close, 23 Nov 2026), a discounted cash flow model with a 9.65% cost of capital does not reach the price at any revenue growth up to 30% a year for five years at the FY26 operating margin of 28.2%; nor, with revenue growing at its FY23–FY26 rate of 10.8%, at any operating margin up to 60%.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: That three-year rate is held down by FY24's 1.0%; the two years since grew 19.3% and 12.8%.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: With the other assumptions at base, the valuation is most sensitive to the cost of capital (one percentage point either way: a model value of ₹1,587 to ₹2,533 a share) and to how long DIVISLAB keeps earning high returns on new investment (anywhere from returns equal to its cost of capital to a quarter above its past level: a model value of ₹1,448 to ₹2,050 a share); the Q3 FY27 result will be the next reported quarter.

prices.note: Each series is rebased to 100 on the first common session. Raw exchange prices are not published here (NSE terms).

metrics.label: Market cap
metrics.definition: Price × shares outstanding (share capital ÷ ₹2 face value at 2026-09-30).

metrics.label: P/E (TTM)
metrics.definition: Price ÷ earnings per share over the last four reported quarters (Q3 FY26 – Q2 FY27).

metrics.label: EV / EBIT (TTM)
metrics.definition: Enterprise value (market cap − the net cash and treasury figure below) ÷ operating profit over the last four quarters.

metrics.label: Net cash and treasury
metrics.definition: Cash, bank balances and treasury investments, less lease liabilities, preference shares and minority interests, at 30 Sep 2026.

metrics.label: Operating margin (FY26)
metrics.definition: EBIT ÷ revenue, after depreciation, excluding other income. Sites that quote an EBITDA-based margin show a higher figure.

metrics.label: ROE (FY26)
metrics.definition: Profit for the year ÷ total equity at year end.

metrics.label: ROIC (FY26)
metrics.definition: After-tax EBIT ÷ invested capital at the start of the year. Invested capital excludes about ₹4k crore of cash and treasury.

metrics.label: Revenue growth FY23–FY26
metrics.definition: Compound annual growth of revenue from FY23 to FY26. FY24 alone grew only 1.0%; the two years since grew more.

metrics.label: Cash conversion (FY26)
metrics.definition: Operating cash flow ÷ profit for the year.

metrics.label: Beta vs NIFTY 50
metrics.definition: Sensitivity of DIVISLAB's daily return to the NIFTY 50's, over the two years to the price date.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.what: Revenue grows only at FY26's pace for five years, the operating margin slips 2 points, and growth after year 10 earns no more than its cost of capital.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.what: Revenue keeps its FY23-FY26 growth rate for five years, the FY26 margin holds, and DIVISLAB keeps its historical return on capital indefinitely.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.what: Revenue grows at H1 FY27's year-on-year pace for five years and the margin rises 1 point.

flags.title: The price is beyond what the model can reach
flags.text: The model cannot reach the price at any revenue growth up to 30% a year, so the page says 'more than 30%' instead of forcing a number. No operating margin up to 60% reaches it either. This is a statement about the model's range and assumptions, not a forecast and not a view on the shares.

flags.title: The exchange's files contain errors
flags.text: 5 reconciliation checks fail on the exchange's own files, each with a recorded reason. They are marked as explained, not passed, and the figure as filed is used, never a corrected one.

flags.title: Foreign exchange is netted per period
flags.text: Divi's reports foreign exchange gains in other income and losses in other expenses, net for each period, so a half year's other income and other expenses can differ from the sum of its two quarters. Profit does not.

flags.title: Lease lines read from scans
flags.text: Lease lines come from scanned results documents. They were machine-read and checked against the printed subtotals, and are marked as not yet checked by a person.

limitations: Template A (non-financial, positive free cash flow). Single-stage fade model; no currency driver.
Cash flows are discounted to the balance-sheet date, 30 Sep 2026, two months before the price date; the model does not roll that gap forward, so its values are slightly low against the price.
The base growth anchor includes FY24's unusually weak year; later years grew faster.
Leases are the only debt; earmarked bank balances are counted as cash, which overstates cash slightly.
The risk-free rate is a twelve-month average while the price and equity risk premium are point-in-time.
The event study measures the size of a move, not its cause; five results days are too few for statistical claims.

Divi's exchange XBRL files do not itemise lease liabilities before the September 2026 half year. The lease lines for March 2022 to March 2026 come from the results PDFs, which are scanned documents: the figures were machine-read and checked against the printed subtotals. The amounts are very small next to the company's size.
Divi's results for FY23 are printed in INR lakh; lines taken from that PDF are converted to INR crore by the engine.

Divi's shows a foreign exchange gain in other income and a loss in other expenses, net for each period, so a half year's other income and other expenses can differ from the sum of its two quarters; profit does not.

At the valuation date the model does not reach the share price at any revenue growth or operating margin inside the ranges it searches. That is a statement about the model's ranges and assumptions, not a view on the shares.
Static page: prices are end-of-day as of the date shown, not live.
